html: 1 July 2013; the former FÁS training centre in Galway came under GRETB in July 2014 (QQI provider profile 2021). Second largest ETB by area; serves a population of over 346,446 (CSO 2022); 2025 budget estimated at about €153m with around 2,000 staff (Annual Report 2024; Service Plan 2025)

David Leahy (named as CE in the Annual Report 2024 and signed the Service Plan 2025 on 31 Jan 2025); Chairperson Cllr Michael Maher (Annual Report 2024)
Strategy Statement 2022–2026 (PDF) · document page Approved Dec 2021. Four goals: People, Programmes, Process, Potential. Annual actions in the Service Plan 2025
Annual Report 2024 (PDF) (financial statements were still subject to C&AG audit at publication)

2024: 18,193 distinct FET learners and 25,615 beneficiaries (Annual Report 2024; the Service Plan 2025 table gives 18,863 and 26,179 for the same year, so the two documents differ). 2025 priorities include College of the Future planning (second preliminary business case submitted Jan 2025), Tertiary degree pathways with ATU, TUS and University of Galway, and Skills to Advance. FET Director: Sinead Morgan (QQI report, Feb 2026). Programmes approved in 2025 included Level 5 Dementia Care and Support, Level 6 Sustainability Leadership, Level 4 Introduction to AI, Level 5 Enhancing Productivity with AI and Level 6 Corporate Sustainability Reporting

2024 beneficiaries: 536 in Phase 2 apprenticeships and 124 in post-2016 apprenticeships (Annual Report 2024). Commis Chef apprenticeship began in Athenry, Hairdressing in Roscommon, and Electrical provision expanded at Mervue with nine new workshops (Annual Report 2024). Hairdressing is run with LCETB and Commis Chef with Kerry ETB (QQI report, Feb 2026)

2024: 1,820 distinct learners and 2,609 beneficiaries in adult literacy groups (Annual Report 2024); the Service Plan 2025 commits to continued implementation of the 10-year Adult Literacy, Numeracy and Digital Skills Strategy

TEL Hub completed; Brickfield accessibility plug-in secured for Moodle; QQI Blended Learning application submitted (QQI report, Feb 2026; Annual Report 2024). Service Plan 2025 plans an AI Committee and guiding principles for AI use

2024 emissions: 2,192,464 kg CO₂, a 23.2% reduction on the 2016–2018 baseline; fossil CO₂ 1,166,534 kg (1.2% reduction). Meeting 2030 targets needs a further 57.2% cut in total CO₂ and 50.4% in fossil CO₂ from 2024 levels. First Climate Action Roadmap, a Climate and Sustainability Champion and school Green Teams in 2024 (Annual Report 2024)

Public Sector Duty built on six values: Dignity, Autonomy, Participation, Inclusion, Social Justice and Environmental Justice, with an action plan in place. Board was 43% female at 31 Dec 2024 (Annual Report 2024)
